options.A: The insured failing to disclose a prior claim history
options.B: The insurer failing to explain clearly the scope and exclusions of the policy to the insured
options.C: The insured inflating the value of a claim
options.D: The insured failing to renew the policy on time

questions.explanation: Utmost good faith is a mutual obligation. The insurer must also act in good faith - for example, by not concealing policy terms, explaining exclusions clearly, and not misrepresenting coverage during the sales process.

questions.stem: Business interruption insurance covers:

options.A: Physical damage to business premises
options.B: Loss of profits and ongoing fixed costs following an insured physical damage event
options.C: Personal accident cover for the business owner
options.D: Legal liability arising from product defects

questions.explanation: Business interruption (consequential loss) insurance indemnifies businesses for loss of income and continuing fixed expenses during the period of interruption following damage to their premises by an insured peril.

questions.stem: The principle of 'insurable interest' in a creditor-debtor relationship means that a creditor:

options.A: Can insure the debtor's life for any amount they choose
options.B: Can insure the debtor's life only to the extent of the outstanding debt
options.C: Has no insurable interest in the life of the debtor under any circumstances
options.D: Must obtain the debtor's written consent before taking out any insurance

questions.explanation: A creditor has an insurable interest in the life of the debtor limited to the amount of the debt. The insurable interest is financial - the creditor stands to lose only the amount owed, not an unlimited amount.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a function of the National Insurance Commission (NAICOM)?

options.A: Licensing and regulation of insurance companies
options.B: Setting minimum capital requirements for insurers
options.C: Providing direct insurance coverage to the public
options.D: Ensuring policyholder protection and market conduct

questions.explanation: NAICOM is a regulatory body - it does not underwrite insurance or provide coverage directly to the public. Its functions are supervisory: licensing, regulating, setting standards, and protecting policyholders.

questions.stem: A 'franchise deductible' in insurance differs from a 'straight deductible' in that:

options.A: It applies only to marine policies
options.B: If the loss exceeds the franchise threshold, the insurer pays the full loss; a straight deductible is always subtracted from the claim payment
options.C: It increases with the age of the policy
options.D: The insurer and insured split the franchise amount equally

questions.explanation: With a franchise deductible, once the loss exceeds the franchise threshold, the entire loss (from the first dollar) is paid by the insurer. A straight deductible is always deducted from the payout regardless of the loss size.

questions.stem: A 'blanket policy' in property insurance covers:

options.A: A single, specifically described item of property
options.B: Multiple items or locations under a single sum insured without specifying individual values
options.C: Only the personal belongings of the insured's family members
options.D: Properties belonging to different owners under a single policy

questions.explanation: A blanket policy covers multiple properties or items under one aggregate sum insured, without allocating specific values to each item. It offers flexibility but may raise average clause issues if the total is inadequate.

questions.stem: A 'specific policy' in property insurance is one that:

options.A: Covers all property without specifying individual items
options.B: Covers a specifically described item or property for a stated sum insured
options.C: Provides coverage for specifically listed named perils only
options.D: Is issued only for properties in specific high-risk locations

questions.explanation: A specific policy covers a particular item or property at a stated sum insured. Each item is individually identified and valued, making it clearer and more precise than a blanket policy.

questions.stem: The 'duty of care' concept in liability insurance refers to:

options.A: The insurer's duty to investigate all claims impartially
options.B: The legal obligation to take reasonable precautions not to cause harm to others
options.C: The insured's duty to care for insured property to prevent losses
options.D: The regulator's duty to monitor the financial health of insurers

questions.explanation: Duty of care is a fundamental concept in negligence law. A person owes a duty of care to those foreseeably affected by their actions. Breach of this duty causing harm gives rise to a liability claim - covered by liability insurance.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the insurance industry in Nigeria is CORRECT?

options.A: The insurance sector in Nigeria is unregulated and operates entirely on market forces
options.B: NAICOM regulates the industry under the Insurance Act 2003 and related legislation
options.C: All insurance companies in Nigeria are owned by the Federal Government
options.D: Foreign insurance companies are not permitted to operate in Nigeria under any circumstances

questions.explanation: Nigeria's insurance sector is regulated by NAICOM (National Insurance Commission) under the Insurance Act 2003, the National Insurance Commission Act, and other enabling legislation, ensuring policyholder protection and market stability.
